marks.gloss_en: היינו דאמרי אינשי: כפין עניא ולא ידע -- the saying fits his having been hungry without knowing it
אי נמי: רווחא לבסימא שכיח -- alternatively, room is always found for the sweet
Abaye: this is what people say: the poor man is hungry and does not know it
R' Oshaya: you have fulfilled through us, our master, 'and sending portions one to another'
Rabba sent Marei bar Mar, by Abaye's hand, a sack full of dates and a cup full of roasted flour
he [Marei bar Mar] sent back a sack full of ginger and a cup full of long pepper

Abaye: when I left the master's house I was sated; when I arrived there they served me sixty plates of sixty kinds of cooked dish and I ate sixty portions of them; the last dish they called pot roast, and I wanted to chew the plate after it
Abaye bar Avin [with R' Chanina bar Avin] would exchange their meals with each other
Rava: a person is obligated to become intoxicated on Purim until he does not know between 'cursed is Haman' and 'blessed is Mordechai'

Rabba and R' Zeira made the Purim feast together; they became drunk; Rabba rose and slaughtered R' Zeira; the next day he prayed for mercy and revived him. The next year he said: let the master come and we will make the Purim feast together
Rava: a Purim feast that one ate at night -- he has not discharged his obligation
the mishna names punishment as the ONLY difference, so in payments the two are alike (marker: the bare הא; see header)
it follows that with regard to payments, this one and that one are equal
דתניא: R' Nechunya ben HaKana makes Yom Kippur like Shabbat for payments -- the equality the mishna implies
whose is the mishna? It is R' Nechunya ben HaKana's
דתניא, רבי יצחק אומר: karet for one's sister was singled out to sentence her to karet and not to lashes
הא מני -- רבי יצחק היא, דאמר מלקות בחייבי כריתות ליכא: the mishna is R' Yitzchak's, for whom there are no lashes where there is karet, so it says nothing about whether lashes exempt from karet
Rav Nachman: whose is this [mishna]? It is R' Yitzchak's

תנינא: the mishna sets Yom Kippur's karet against Shabbat's punishment at the hand of man; if lashes (at the hand of man) exempted from karet, both would be at the hand of man -- so the mishna's tanna disagrees with R' Chananya ben Gamliel
bei Rav: we have learned it -- the mishna contrasts Shabbat (at the hand of man) with Yom Kippur (karet); were [R' Chananya ben Gamliel's ruling] so, both would be at the hand of man
אפילו תימא רבנן: זה עיקר זדונו בידי אדם וזה עיקר זדונו בהיכרת -- even on the Rabbis' view the mishna speaks of each day's PRIMARY punishment, so it is no proof against R' Chananya ben Gamliel
Rav Ashi: even if you say [the mishna is] the Rabbis' -- [it means] this one's primary deliberate violation is at the hand of man, and that one's primary deliberate violation is with karet
there is no difference between Shabbat and Yom Kippur except that this one's deliberate violation is [punished] at the hand of man and that one's with karet
all those liable to karet who were flogged are exempted from their karet
אין בין ... אלא אוכל נפש בלבד -- הא לענין מכשירי אוכל נפש זה וזה שוין
hence with regard to facilitators of food preparation, this [Yom Tov] and that [Shabbat] are alike -- they are forbidden on Yom Tov too
דתניא: אין בין יום טוב לשבת אלא אוכל נפש; רבי יהודה מתיר אף מכשירי אוכל נפש (kind tanya_kevatei: no kind names a bare דתניא)
the mishna is not in accordance with R' Yehuda
ואידך נמי, הכתיב לכם? -- and the first tanna too: is 'for you' not written [which R' Yehuda reads as 'for all your needs']?
לכם ולא לגוים, לכם ולא לכלבים -- he uses 'for you' to exclude gentiles and dogs (= p_lachem_velo_legoyim)
the first tanna reads 'for you': for you and not for gentiles, for you and not for dogs
ואידך נמי, הא כתיב הוא? -- and R' Yehuda too: is 'that' not written [which the first tanna reads as 'and not its facilitators']?
כתיב הוא וכתיב לכם: כאן במכשירין שאפשר לעשותן מערב יום טוב, כאן במכשירין שאי אפשר לעשותן מערב יום טוב (= p_ry_efshar_asur, p_ry_ee_efshar_mutar)
R' Yehuda: 'that' is written and 'for you' is written -- here [הוא], facilitators that can be done on the eve of Yom Tov [are forbidden]
the mishna: there is no difference between Yom Tov and Shabbat except food preparation alone
the first tanna's reason: the verse says 'that [alone may be done for you]' (Ex 12:16) -- 'that', and not its facilitators
